D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the full stack comprehensively — Django/DRF backend, React frontend, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS deployment, CI/CD, and DSA woven throughout all 10 months. It includes a progressive blog project and a capstone (e-commerce/social platform) with deployment, plus dedicated interview prep in Month 10 with mock interviews and system design. Plan 2 also covers the full stack but front-loads DRF in Month 1 (skipping foundational Django review), delays DSA to Months 6-7, and introduces a new portfolio project only in Month 9 with limited time to complete it. Plan 1's capstone is more ambitious and employer-worthy, with explicit AWS deployment and CI/CD. Plan 2's portfolio strategy is weaker — the 'new ambitious project' in Month 9 leaves only one month to complete and polish it. Both include behavioral prep, but Plan 1 has more explicit mock interview scheduling and system design coverage.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 delivers a more employer-worthy capstone with full deployment, integrates DSA throughout rather than siloing it, and has more structured mock interview and system design preparation.

core_technical_readiness.justification: Covers Django/DRF, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, CI/CD, Git — all core full-stack requirements. Depth is appropriate for a graduate-level hire. Minor gap: Redis/Celery not covered.

interview_prep_readiness.justification: DSA integrated monthly from Month 1, system design introduced in Month 7 and deepened in Month 10, mock interviews explicitly scheduled in Month 10, behavioral prep via STAR method. Strong coverage across all SWE interview pillars.

portfolio_project_strength.justification: Two projects: a Django blog (with DRF, auth, PostgreSQL) and a capstone (e-commerce/social platform) deployed to AWS with CI/CD. Progressive build, live deployment, and professional READMEs planned. Highly employer-worthy.

core_technical_readiness.justification: Covers Django/DRF, React, PostgreSQL, Docker basics, deployment, Redis/Celery, and web security (OWASP). Good breadth but Month 8 advanced topics feel rushed given the 1hr/day constraint.

interview_prep_readiness.justification: DSA is siloed to Months 6-7 with no integration into earlier months, reducing retention. System design is covered in Month 9 but briefly. Mock interviews mentioned in Month 10 but not structured. Less consistent interview prep cadence.

portfolio_project_strength.justification: Integrated full-stack app deployed in Month 5 is good, but the 'new ambitious project' starting in Month 9 leaves only ~30 hours to build, document, and polish it. Risk of incomplete or under-documented capstone at job application time.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 explicitly budgets 216 planned hours with 24 buffer hours out of 240 total, and breaks down each month into theory, practice, and project hours. This is transparent and realistic. However, some months pack a lot — e.g., Month 1 covers advanced Git, advanced Python OOP, SOLID principles, AND foundational DSA in 22 hours, which is ambitious for 1hr/day. Plan 2 claims ~300 hours total for a 1hr/day, 10-month plan, which is mathematically incorrect (10 months × 30 days × 1hr = ~300 hours is plausible only if counting every single day including weekends). Plan 2 does not provide per-month hour budgets, making feasibility harder to verify. Plan 2's Month 1 jumping straight into DRF, JWT, and advanced PostgreSQL without reviewing Django fundamentals may be too steep. Plan 2's Month 8 stacks Redis, Celery, advanced ORM, Redux, testing, and OWASP security — clearly overloaded for ~30 hours.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 1 provides explicit hour budgets with a buffer, making feasibility verifiable, while Plan 2 has an inflated hour claim and a severely overloaded Month 8.

hour_compliance.justification: 216 planned hours + 24 buffer = 240 total. Matches the 10-month, 1hr/day constraint precisely. Transparent monthly breakdown provided.

cognitive_load_realism.justification: Most months are reasonable, but Month 1 (advanced Git + advanced Python + OOP/SOLID + DSA) and Month 3 (Django views + PostgreSQL + DRF intro + DSA trees) are dense for 22 hours. Some weeks may require more than 1 hour to complete meaningfully.

overengineering_avoidance.justification: AWS EC2/RDS/S3/Route53 + Nginx + CI/CD in Month 9 is ambitious but justified for a production-ready portfolio. Trimmed topics are explicitly justified. Minor concern with Dijkstra's algorithm inclusion given time constraints.

hour_compliance.justification: Claims ~300 hours for 1hr/day over 10 months, which overstates available hours (realistically ~240-300 depending on daily consistency). No per-month hour breakdown makes compliance unverifiable.

overengineering_avoidance.justification: SASS/SCSS, Redis, Celery, Zustand, and OWASP Top 10 are included but feel like scope creep for a 1hr/day plan. The new ambitious project in Month 9 alongside system design study is unrealistic.

Plan 1 explicitly justifies skipping Kotlin/C/C++ and explains why Python/JavaScript is the focus, and it builds on the user's existing Django knowledge rather than restarting from scratch. Plan 1 also explicitly addresses remote work preparation (LinkedIn optimization, networking, elevator pitch). Plan 2 also leverages Python/Django but jumps to DRF in Month 1 without acknowledging that the user may need some Django consolidation first. Plan 2 mentions English communication as advice for global remote roles, which is a thoughtful personalization touch. Both plans use the user's preferred Python stack, but Plan 1 provides more explicit rationale for technology choices and better addresses the remote job context throughout the plan.

D4.name: Market Alignment
D4.comparative_analysis: Both plans cover the globally in-demand full-stack skill set: Python/Django backend, React frontend, PostgreSQL, Docker, and cloud deployment. Plan 1 includes AWS (EC2, RDS, S3) which is more globally recognized than Heroku/Render (Plan 2's primary deployment option), and CI/CD via GitHub Actions. Plan 2 includes Redis, Celery, and OWASP security awareness, which are valuable differentiators for senior-leaning roles but may be premature for a graduate-level hire. Plan 1's AWS focus is more aligned with global enterprise hiring. Both plans include system design, which is standard for SWE interviews globally. Neither plan includes TypeScript, which is increasingly expected in global remote roles, but this is a minor gap given the time constraint.
D4.winner_reason: Plan 1's AWS deployment focus is more globally marketable than Heroku/Render, and its skill set is better calibrated for graduate-level global remote hiring.

skill_demand_relevance.justification: Django/DRF, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, CI/CD, Git — all highly in-demand globally for full-stack roles. Missing TypeScript and Redis, but appropriate for the timeline. AWS is a strong differentiator.

D5.name: Strategic Prioritization Quality
D5.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 follows a coherent arc: Foundation (Git, Python, DSA basics) → Backend (Django, DRF, PostgreSQL) → Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS, React) → Integration → Deployment → Interview Blitz. DSA is woven throughout, ensuring retention. The blog project builds progressively into a capstone. Plan 2's phasing has a notable issue: it front-loads DRF and advanced backend in Month 1, then does frontend in Months 2-4, deployment in Month 5, then pivots entirely to DSA in Months 6-7, then advanced framework topics in Month 8, then system design + new project in Month 9. This creates a disjointed arc where DSA is siloed and the new portfolio project starts too late. Plan 1's integrated DSA approach and progressive project building is strategically superior.
D5.winner_reason: Plan 1's integrated DSA approach and progressive project arc is more strategically coherent than Plan 2's siloed DSA block and late-starting new portfolio project.

high_roi_topics_prioritized.justification: Backend API skills (highest ROI for full-stack) are prioritized early. DSA starts Month 1 for sustained practice. React comes after backend foundation is solid. Minor concern: frontend starts Month 5, which is relatively late.

high_roi_topics_prioritized.justification: DRF front-loaded in Month 1 is good for ROI, but DSA delayed to Months 6-7 means 5 months without interview prep practice. New portfolio project starting Month 9 is a low-ROI timing decision.

D6.name: Curriculum Structural Depth & Clarity

Each month has a named milestone deliverable. The level of detail is significantly higher than Plan 2. Plan 2 provides monthly topics, activities, and a single output statement per month, plus a consolidated resource list. Plan 2's structure is clear but less granular — topics are listed without weekly breakdown, and activities are somewhat generic. Plan 1's weekly micro-goals make it immediately actionable, while Plan 2 requires the user to self-organize within each month.
D6.winner_reason: Plan 1's weekly micro-goals, per-month hour budgets, specific deliverables, and curated resources per topic provide significantly more actionable structure than Plan 2's monthly topic lists.

D7.name: Career Execution Readiness
D7.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 integrates job hunt action items every single month — LinkedIn optimization in Month 1, company research in Month 2, networking in Month 3, resume updates in Month 4, personal website in Month 5, system design reading in Month 6, portfolio updates in Month 7, elevator pitch in Month 8, resume refinement in Month 9, and full application hustle in Month 10. Mock interviews are explicitly scheduled in Month 10 with peer/mentor feedback. Plan 2 consolidates all career execution into Month 10, with resume/LinkedIn, behavioral prep, mock interviews, and job applications all crammed into the final month. This is a significant weakness — career preparation should be progressive, not a last-minute sprint.
D7.winner_reason: Plan 1 distributes career execution actions across all 10 months, while Plan 2 dangerously concentrates all job search preparation into the final month.

Its weekly micro-goals, integrated DSA practice, progressive portfolio building, AWS deployment, and month-by-month career execution actions make it significantly more likely to result in a job offer within the 10-month window.
